newsitem.title: USA: IPO SPOTLIGHT - Snyder Communications debut.
newsitem.headline: IPO SPOTLIGHT - Snyder Communications debut.

text.p: Snyder Communications Inc's initial public offering this week should find favor in the reviving IPO market, according to several analysts.
"It's a good, solid deal -- I expect a minimum premium of two points at the opening." said Vincent Slavin, who tracks IPOs for Cantor Fitzgerald.

David Menlow, president of Springfield, N.J.-based IPO Financial Network Corp, echoes this view. "The market is going to go for this (deal)," he said. "We're looking at a 10 percent premium at opening."
"There is sex appeal in this," said Menlow. "Outsourced marketing has become a buzzword."

Snyder is an outsourced marketing services provider, designing and implementing marketing programs for its clients through a variety of resources, including field sales, teleservices, wallboard information displays and product sampling.

Both Slavin and Menlow said the IPO market could easily absorb more than the 7.8 million shares currently on offer -- the company had previously planned to offer 12 million shares -- and it was conceivable the deal could be expanded.
According to Merrill Lynch, lead underwriter on the deal, the IPO could price late on Tuesday. The estimated price range is $14 to $16 per share.
Some analysts expressed concern with the company's concentration on its two main clients, AT&T Corp and MCI Communications Corp.
According to the prospectus, AT&T currently accounts for over 50 percent of the company's revenues, and MCI accounts for about 25 percent.
Steven Tuen, analyst at IPO Value Monitor, sees a two-fold problem with this: "One, if AT&T pulls the program, and two, (the fact that) they can't leverage their resources to other competitors."
Under its contract with AT&T, Snyder is precluded from concurrently selling similar telecommunications services for AT&T's competitors to the foreign-origin consumer market in the U.S.
The company had 1995 revenues of $42.9 million, up from $11.7 million in 1994.
